newsitem.title: USA: Calif. governor approves L.A. County breakup study.
newsitem.headline: Calif. governor approves L.A. County breakup study.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson signed legislation Tuesday authorizing a study of the pros and cons of breaking up sprawling Los Angeles County.

The measure, approved by the state legislature in July, will create a local agency, called the Los Angeles County Division Commission, to study proposals to divide up the county into two or three smaller counties.
The commission will issue a report advising state and local lawmakers on the breakup by January 2001.
Several bills have been introduced in Sacramento in recent years to break up Los Angeles County, which has a population of more than nine million people.
Unlike the previous measures, which were highly controversial, the bill signed by Wilson Tuesday only calls for a study of the issue.
